punchline: Intelligence test scores rose because people were not born smarter but learned to look at the world through abstract lenses.
thirty_sec: In the twentieth century, intelligence test scores rose from generation to generation. James Flynn showed that this was tied not to inborn intelligence but to modern people learning to see the world abstractly and scientifically. Villagers who had never been to school spoke of concrete uses instead of abstract categories. According to David Epstein, abstract patterns are the most valuable skill because they can be carried from one field to another.
